# Contraceptives: what's the deal? {data-section="lvl2"}

## What the deal is: {data-section="lvl2"}

**They are important!**

\

Why? 

\

They allow women to control if/when they get pregnant

- Important for equality especially in developing countries

The pill is old. But we keep finding out new things about side effects etc. 

I am investigating: 

- Effects of different contraceptives on diagnosis / medication outcomes 
- Labtest outcomes (not covering it today)

1. How prescriptions are redeemed (more at a time?)

In a database fashion: faster and more memory efficient

## Throught the interface: {data-section="lvl2"}

![](../graphics/logos/tidyverse_logos/hex-stickers/SVG/tidymodels.svg){fig-align="center"}

## Looks something like this: {data-section="lvl2"}

```text
# Set a prior
prior_dist <- rstanarm::student_t(df = 1)


# make the parsnip model
bayes_mod <-   
  linear_reg() %>% 
  set_engine("stan", 
             prior_intercept = prior_dist, 
             prior = prior_dist) 

# train the model
bayes_fit <- 
  bayes_mod %>% 
  fit(width ~ initial_volume * food_regime, data = urchins)
```
